subject: RFP: MeridianHealth assurance package — control linkage & evidence accession plan
messages:
From: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridianhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Meridian RFP - control mapping follow-up

Hi David,

Thanks for the initial submission of the RFP responses. Our security team reviewed the high level answers and asked for a tighter mapping between your controls and Meridian's SOC 2/ISO controls. Specifically: a) canonical control IDs for each RFP line item, b) sample artifacts we can use for our audit (logs, config screenshots), and c) an ingestion plan for any large evidence bundles.

Can you provide a proposed accession plan and a small sample bundle we can vet before we ask our auditors to accept the dataset? Also include any redaction guidance for PII in logs.

Best,
Meredith

MeridianHealth
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-15T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - control mapping follow-up

Meredith —

Thanks for the clear ask. Kimberly and Priyom are copied; we prepared a two-part delivery: 1) a SOC 2 / ISO 27001 crosswalk file that aligns your questionnaire rows to Redwood control IDs and the evidence type (we've attached meridian-soc2-crosswalk.xlsx), and 2) a small evidence sample (logs & config snapshots) packaged as evidence-sample-logs.zip.

High level accession plan:
- Day 0: Share crosswalk + sample bundle (attached).
- Day 1-2: Your security team validates sample; we redact PII using our log-redact pipeline (described in the attached PDF).
- Day 3: Full evidence handoff via SFTP (or secure Drive link) in segmented archives by control family (auth, config, telemetry).
- Day 4-7: Optional remote walk-through and key artifact verification call with our SOC engineer.

We recommend Meridian accept the sample before we open the full bundle to auditors; if you're happy, we'll provide a signed chain-of-custody manifest per archive.

Let us know if SFTP or a managed Drive link works best for you.

-David

--
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridianhealth.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-16T14:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - control mapping follow-up

Meredith — quick note on redaction and artifact scope.

- Redaction: Our pipeline strips sensitive fields (SSNs, patient identifiers, JWTs) and replaces with deterministic tokens. We will provide a redaction report sample that shows the regex patterns and the entropy-preserving token map.
- Artifact types: we plan to include the following by control family:
  * Auth: IAM role definitions, rotation history, KMS keypolicies (sanitized)
  * Telemetry: 14 days of audit/event logs (redacted), request traces (pseudonymized request ids)
  * Runtime: container image digests, runtime flags, quantized model config snapshots
  * Network: VPC flow sample (anonymized IPs)

Attachments included in the sample bundle: deployment-architecture-diagram.png and a 10MB compressed log sample.

If Meridian needs evidence in a specific format (CSV, parquet) for ingestion into your audit tool, tell us the preferred schema and we'll export accordingly.

-Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Arthur Lim <arthur.lim@securethirdparty.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T08:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - control mapping follow-up

David / Kimberly —

Arthur from SecureThirdParty here (we run the evidence extraction collector for several health clients). A quick operational note: when packaging telemetry for healthcare auditors we recommend including an MD5 manifest with chunked archives to speed verifier downloads and a short JSON metadata file per archive describing the control families and time ranges. We can host the SFTP and provide pre-signed transfer tokens if Meridian prefers to avoid Drive transfers.

Happy to align on the manifest template — attaching a sample manifest in the Drive link above.

Arthur
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Meredith Allen <meredith.allen@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Arthur Lim <arthur.lim@securethirdparty.com>
Date: 2027-10-20T16:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - control mapping follow-up

Meredith —

Following up with the full accession proposal. Key asks for Meridian to confirm so we can proceed:
1) Accept the sample bundle (meridian-soc2-crosswalk.xlsx + evidence-sample-logs.zip)
2) Preferred transfer mechanism: SFTP hosted by Arthur / SecureThirdParty OR shared Drive (we will encrypt at rest).
3) Auditors: name and contact so we can generate a signed chain-of-custody for their review.

Next steps on our side if you approve: schedule a 30-min intake call (we have availability tomorrow 10–11am PT), provide the manifest template (Arthur will host), and start packaging segmented archives.

Attached: redwood-iso-summary.pdf (controls narrative and redaction checklist).

Thanks — looking forward to the green light.

-David

--
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
